court: The lord's manorial court at Ruislip, Middlesex, in the Bec rolls.
judges: Twelve sworn jurors find the fact; the court (suitors) gives the result, with seisin following the finding in this entry.
begins: A litigant pays the lord for a jury to decide the better right to land: 12d for a headland in this entry. The other party objects that she holds only as guardian of a minor heir and cannot bring the land into judgment.
proof: An inquest by twelve sworn jurors finds the greater right and who receives seisin. The entry is partly cut off in the text read.

sources.title: Maitland, Select Pleas in Manorial and Other Seignorial Courts, vol. 1, Ruislip roll 1248

note: data/procedures/SOURCES.md: the roll is from 1248; use c. 1300 is an inference. Presiding officer and appeal/removal are not stated in the source. The fee and objection describe this entry, not a universal rule. The extracted entry is incomplete.
